title: Myth: every big crocodile is a man-eater

scenes.headline: Every big crocodile is a man-eater.
The gharial is built for fish.
scenes.body: Adults eat mainly fish. The long, thin snout and interlocking teeth are made for gripping slippery prey.

scenes.headline: Males grow a pot-shaped knob on the snout.
scenes.body: It's called a ghara, after the clay pot. Males reach 5–6 m.

scenes.label: adult gharials left in the wild
scenes.body: Critically Endangered. About 77% live along one river: the Chambal.

caption:
The gharial looks fierce, but it's a fish specialist.

Young gharials also eat insects, crustaceans and frogs; adults switch almost entirely to fish.

Sources: Smithsonian's National Zoo; IUCN Red List, Gavialis gangeticus (Lang, Chowfin & Ross 2019). Photo: wild female, Babai River, Bardiya NP. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Myth stated plainly, busted with diet and anatomy, ends on a hard conservation number; one wild photo reframed with focus/crops since media is thin.
